body:
[aida:advisor] #2043 IS HELD, BOTH LAYERS. And the question you said you could not answer from the refs - work lost, or work never produced - is answered. It is NEITHER, and the session did nothing wrong.

HELD FIRST: marker .aida/merge-holds/PR-2043 plus the aida:merge-hold label. Verified both. I confirmed your evidence before acting: #2042 and #2043 both at 35de6d3abb, five commits ahead of main, every one carrying a BUG-1420 or TASK-1289 trailer, none STORY-1391.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, from .aida/headless-logs/story-1391-work-01a0c193-*.jsonl - the same place the destroyed #2040 verdict turned up an hour ago.

The session holding the STORY-1391 lease was handed BUG-1420 ROUND-2 REWORK as its brief. It never attempted STORY-1391 work, so nothing was lost - there was nothing to lose. It then did the BUG-1420 work carefully and, in one respect, better than I would have:

  - it found #2009 was stacked on the stale task-1289-work branch, so updating it would have
    required rewriting that PR's remote history;
  - it explicitly REFUSED the unapproved force-push - its words: "I'm avoiding an unapproved
    force-push";
  - it built a fresh branch off current main with only TASK-1289 and BUG-1420 in scope;
  - it hit a modify/delete conflict cherry-picking 065f3df8aa, worked out that the file belongs
    to still-unmerged TASK-1289, and recorded that rather than, its words again, "silently
    manufacturing a false clean cherry-pick";
  - it pushed local story-1391-work to the REMOTE name bug-1420-round2 and opened #2042 itself.

The log line that explains your byte-identical branches exactly:

    branch 'story-1391-work' set up to track 'origin/bug-1420-round2'

So the two refs are the same because one session pushed one branch under an honest remote name. #2042 was created 01:32:04Z by the implementer. #2043 was created 01:33:50Z - one minute forty-six later - from the local branch NAME, by the orchestrator, after the implementer had already published. #2043 is a duplicate PR of #2042, not a rival implementation.

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT BRANCH SELECTION AND NOT DATA LOSS. It is two things:
  a. A session was leased STORY-1391 and briefed BUG-1420. The lease and the brief disagreed, and
     nothing checked that they matched.
  b. The orchestrator opened a second PR from the lease's branch name without noticing the
     implementer had already opened one for the same head.

MY RECOMMENDATION, and the call on the in-flight run is yours since you own dispatch: #2042 lives, #2043 closes. Not merged, not reworked - closed as a duplicate. I have not closed it, because the drain is at phase 2 on it and I would rather not pull a PR out from under a running phase without you deciding how to stop the run.

ONE THING I DID DO: STORY-1391 was status DONE with nothing implemented, which is the harm your point 1 described, already realised. I moved it back to Approved. Its acceptance - detecting that a finding survived a round - is untouched work and it should go back through the queue properly. Pulling it from batch:night-0920 was right; it needs a brief that matches its lease next time.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the implementer session in this incident refused a force-push it had not been authorised to make, diagnosed a cross-spec dependency correctly, and declined to fake a clean cherry-pick. The failure is entirely in what it was handed and what was done with its output afterwards. If any of this gets written up, it should not read as an implementer error.
subject: #2043 held both layers - and the log answers your open question: no work lost, the lease and the brief disagreed
